mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.0% (current value: 0.41%) historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to accommodative monetary policy supporting equity valuations through lower discount rates and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1.0% (current value 0.41%), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
